newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ecopetrol sets force majeure on crude transport.
newsitem.headline: Ecopetrol sets force majeure on crude transport.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol has declared force majeure on the transport of crude along the country's largest pipeline, a company spokesman said Monday.

The move came after the pipeline, which runs from the Cano Limon field in northeast Arauca province to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas, was blown up twice and partially destroyed by a landslide over the weekend.
"We took the decision because of the serious nature of the damage which will not be repaired until at least Friday," an Ecopetrol spokesman said.
He stressed, however, that no decision had yet been taken on whether to declare force majeure on liftings and export of crude.
"We're still evaluating what our lifting schedules are and how much crude we have in storage at Covenas," he said.

Occidental petroleum Corp OXY.N, which operates the Cano Limon field which produces about 175,000 barrels per day, seems almost certain to shut in production at the field and is also mulling force majeure -- a decision was due to be announced later Monday. Occidental has capacity to store only about three full days output on site and pumping along the pipeline has already been suspended since Wednesday after an earlier pipeline bombing.
